- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and news volume remains high, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lingering momentum.
- Model underperforms when sentiment volatility is high (rapid changes) — adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% for each 0.33 drop in sentiment magnitude.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-cycle rallies; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for days 25–30 if sentiment is rising or news volume >2.5.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is low and price is rising, model often fails to recognize momentum — increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for 2–3 days to avoid lag.
